pr_text:
fix(price): make adapter and fan-out drops visible and bounded (R-W18, W1-8 retro); logging only, unflagged

DEFECTS (from the retro adversary review of PR #143, reproduced as probes P1-P5):
- W1-8b: _curl_scraper, _firecrawl_scraper and _scrapedo_scraper swallow their fetch exception at DEBUG. Prod runs LOG_LEVEL=INFO, so a fan-out where every scraper failed looks the same as one where every scraper missed. fan_out's failed_count stays 0 for them and nothing reads it.
- W1-8c: the three consume `except asyncio.TimeoutError` branches (sitemap, jsonapi, the _new_adapter_specs loop) are silent, so a budget-clamped consume under the genuine-priority flag drops a whole family with no line. _timeout_none cannot see an inner timeout the adapter swallowed (M13-34 clamps inner fetches to 9 s under the 10 s wrap). It also logs a TimeoutError the adapter raised 10 ms in as `TIMEOUT after 10.0s`.
- W1-8d: the ERROR drop line writes str(exc) verbatim. Probe P4 gave a 200,136-character record containing a proxy password and a raw newline.

FIX (app/services/structured_comparison_service.py only; no return value changes):
- Per-scraper failure, one INFO line: `[ADAPTER DROP] fanout:<curl|firecrawl|scrapedo>:<retailer_domain>: ERROR <Type>: <_safe_exc text>`. It carries the retailer label as the scraper receives it, never the scraped URL. The DEBUG `{url} raised` lines are gone.
- Per-wave summary after fan_out returns: `[FANOUT] wave=<curl|render> completed=N failed=N cancelled=N elapsed=S`, where completed = wave size - failed - cancelled.
- On the wave's budget TimeoutError: `[FANOUT] wave=<kind> TIMEOUT pending=N elapsed=S`, where pending = wave size (fan_out's own counts are lost when it is cancelled).
- Consume branches: `[ADAPTER DROP] <sitemap|jsonapi|woo|salla|occ|...>: CONSUME-BOUND after <bound>s`. The bound is the one actually waited under, captured with a walrus at the existing `_consume_bound()` call.
- _timeout_none is timed with time.monotonic():
  - wrap timeout, logged only when elapsed >= timeout - 0.05: `TIMEOUT after <elapsed>s`
  - earlier TimeoutError: `ERROR TimeoutError (adapter-raised)`
  - None at or after adapter_inner_ceiling() - 0.5: `SLOW-MISS after <elapsed>s`
  - fast misses and every hit stay silent; cancellation is still never caught and never logged.
- New local `_safe_exc(exc)`: it removes URL userinfo up to the last '@' before the host, drops the query string and fragment, and keeps host and path. Every line break (including U+2028/U+2029 and \x0b) becomes one space, and the text is cut to 200 chars. It scrubs before truncating. It is applied to the _timeout_none ERROR line and to the new fanout lines.
  - Why not the W1-1 helper: it was measured to be unfit. sentry_service._scrub_query_string keeps api_key= and never strips userinfo.

FAILED_COUNT IS NOT THE PRODUCTION SIGNAL. failed_count keeps its semantics. Production scrapers still catch their fetch errors and return None, so the summary's failed= stays 0 for real fetch failures; only an exception that escapes a scraper (a bug) raises it. The production failure signal is the per-scraper `[ADAPTER DROP] fanout:` lines. The W5 STEP-0 canary must count `[ADAPTER DROP] fanout:` lines (and `CONSUME-BOUND` / `SLOW-MISS` / `TIMEOUT` lines), not failed=.

FLAG ROW: none. The fix is unflagged because the reviewer found silent drops with no legitimate reader, and the change only adds log lines.

ACTIVATION GATE: live on deploy. Nothing to flip. Before reading W5 canaries off these lines, watch log volume during the first slow-source episode: at most one line per dropped adapter or scraper, plus one [FANOUT] line per wave. Volume is UNMEASURED; the earlier review estimated about 18 drop lines per product at worst, and this unit adds up to 2 [FANOUT] lines per product plus one fanout drop per failed scraper URL. price-warmer runs stale 2026-09-02 code and emits none of this until redeployed.

EVIDENCE:
- Unit: tests/test_retro_w1_8.py plus tests/test_adapter_drop_visibility.py, 33/33 passed on the pinned venv with an autouse zero-network guard.
- Mutation matrix: 34/34 KILLED from sha-verified byte snapshots, with unmutated controls passing.
- Comm gate: the 152-file module-reference set under the netguard plugin gives 2 failed / 3963 passed, identical to base 1c6f6796. branch-only-NEW is empty, and both failures are in tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt.
- Lint: ruff E9,F63,F7,F82 and py_compile are clean.

HONEST LIMITS:
- pending= on the wave TimeoutError branch is the wave size, an upper bound. Scrapers that already missed before the budget cancel are counted as pending, because fan_out's internal task state is not reachable without changing price_service (out of scope).
- A fanout ERROR line keeps any host and path that appear inside the exception's own text, with userinfo and query stripped. The scraped URL argument itself is never logged.
- `<retailer_domain>` is the harvest label (it can be a subdomain such as bahrain.sharafdg.com); no eTLD+1 is computed.
- SLOW-MISS keys on adapter_inner_ceiling(), which defaults to 8.5 s. An adapter that swallows a SHORTER inner timeout of its own (for example a 3 s leg) still reads as a fast miss.
- An instant curl_cffi Timeout stays silent by design (ruling 1).
- CONSUME-BOUND says the family was cut. It does not name which sources inside the family were still pending, because the cancelled per-source tasks stay unlogged by design.

FOLLOW-UPS, not in this unit:
- Log volume measurement on the first canary.
- An exact pending count needs fan_out to expose per-task state (price_service change).
- The reviewer's unaddressed minor: the PR #143 body's byte-identity citation (9504e5... / non_none=825) is environment-dependent and cannot detect a W1-8 regression. Future byte-identity claims should cite a same-env parent-vs-head pair only.
- The two tests the reviewer marked as proving nothing about production (test_fan_out_reports_failed_count_separately_from_cancelled, test_failed_count_sees_a_raiser_done_but_never_yielded) are kept as counting pins. Production visibility is now pinned by the scraper-level tests in test_retro_w1_8.py.
- Redeploy price-warmer to pick this up.

Seven green-phase nodes were added: _safe_exc edge shapes, the fanout lines going through _safe_exc for all three scrapers, the completed arithmetic, and a TIMEOUT line that reports the measured elapsed rather than the wrap. The last one exists because a mutation that logged {timeout} instead of elapsed would otherwise have survived; the pin makes it KILLED (M29).

The fanout ERROR line appends `: <_safe_exc(e)>` after `ERROR <Type>`, following ruling 2 (_safe_exc applied to the new fanout lines). The ruling-3 token is therefore a prefix, and the tests accept exactly that token plus an optional `: ...` tail.
_safe_exc also drops URL fragments along with the query string (fragments can carry tokens) and collapses every Unicode line break, not only \n and \r, so the line stays grep-stable.
`pending=` on the TimeoutError branch is the wave size (upper bound), not a live pending count; see residual risk.
The TIMEOUT/SLOW-MISS elapsed values are printed with 2 decimals, for example `TIMEOUT after 0.30s`, where the old line printed the configured wrap (`10.0s`).

residual_risk:
1. INFO log volume under a slow-source episode is unmeasured. The worst case is one line per failed fan-out scraper URL, plus per-source adapter drops, plus up to 2 [FANOUT] lines and up to about 9 CONSUME-BOUND lines per product.

2. pending= is an upper bound, not a live count.

3. An exception's own text can still carry a retailer host and path, with userinfo, query and fragment stripped and 200 chars max. The regex strips userinfo only when it is followed by '@' in the same whitespace-free token, so a password split by a space would not be recognised as userinfo. That is a malformed URL; no adapter has been seen to produce one.

4. The summary's failed= stays 0 for production fetch failures by design. A canary that reads failed= instead of counting `[ADAPTER DROP] fanout:` lines will undercount. This is stated in pr_text.

5. SLOW-MISS keys on adapter_inner_ceiling() - 0.5 (8.5 s by default). Adapters with a shorter private inner timeout still look like fast misses.

6. The comm gate ran against the recorded red-phase BASE with an extra warm-up plugin on HEAD only. The plugin changes import timing, not outcomes.

7. The 34-mutation matrix for M04-M34 ran in scratch copies of app/ and the two test files. M01-M03 ran in the worktree. Controls in each copy passed first.

8. Scratch artefacts left under scratchpad/rw18_green: mutroot_1..3 copies, snapshots and logs. Nothing was recursively deleted, per the rules.
